Connectivity module for BactoSense and BactoSense Multi. This edition describes the BactoHub workflow and is valid from BactoSense software 2.2.

BactoLink establishes a remote connection between the instrument and your PC. Initiate the connection through the BactoHub portal using HTTPS and a web browser. The portal is the access point for BactoLink and the associated instruments. A connection remains active for 30 minutes and must then be re-established.

Additional information Information notices provide additional details about the current topic. Numbered lists describe practical procedures. Screenshots are examples and may differ from the current device.

BactoLink consists of an antenna, an Ethernet cable and a Power-over-Ethernet (PoE) injector. The injector connects to the BactoSense or BactoSense Multi power supply. Before installation: Check that the instrument runs software 2.2 or later. Activate DHCP and HTTPS in the instrument settings. Activate VNC if GUI relay is required. Make sure you have an account at hub.bnovate.com. Request an account from support@bnovate.com if needed.

The PoE injector powers the antenna through Ethernet. Its Ethernet and power connections to the instrument are permanently integrated. It has a port for the power cable supplied with BactoSense, and an Ethernet connection to the antenna. The injector height from its feet to its top is 65.5 mm. Mechanical specification Value Material Polycarbonate (PC) Connectors RJ45, power connector Protection IP67 Dimensions, L × H × W 165 × 165 × 54 mm Operating temperature 5–30 °C

The antenna connects to the PoE injector through Ethernet and houses the SIM card for mobile connections (4G/LTE, 3G, 2G). See Mounting BactoLink for the mounting bracket. Mechanical specification Value Materials ABS, PC, FR4 Connector RJ45 Protection IP67 Dimensions, L × H × W 165 × 165 × 54 mm Weight 0.8 kg Operating temperature −40–80 °C

Connection Description 1 Ethernet between the PoE injector and the instrument's RJ45 port 2 Power between the PoE injector and the instrument's power port 3 Ethernet between the PoE injector and the antenna 4 Power supply to the PoE injector. The power supply is delivered with BactoSense.

Open the bag containing the Ethernet cable. Open the PoE injector package and its separate connector bag. Take out the cap, sealing ring with opening, spacer and connector to the PoE injector. Line them up on the Ethernet cable as illustrated. Guide the RJ45 connector into the PoE connector. Both allow only one orientation. Push the RJ45 connector as far forward as possible. Push the spacer and sealing ring into the PoE connector. Screw the cap on while gently pushing the parts together, until hand-tight. The resulting fitting is a bayonet fitting to the PoE injector. Align the other end of the Ethernet cable in front of you. Take the antenna connector and O-ring from the antenna package. Unscrew the antenna connector and push out the sealing ring. If necessary, use the curved mounting rod to push it out. Align the antenna connector parts on the Ethernet cable as illustrated. Assemble the antenna connector in order Connect RJ45 to the antenna first, secure the connector to the antenna, and mount the cap last. This prevents the cable from being locked beneath the seal. Push the RJ45 connector lightly into the antenna connector. Ensure its small tab is within the antenna. Push the sealing ring into the antenna connector. Put the O-ring on the antenna connector and connect RJ45. Screw the connector into the antenna. Screw the cap onto the connector.
documents.s: Connecting the antenna and PoE injector

documents.t: The mounting set attaches the antenna to cylindrical or square objects, pipes or rods. Open the antenna package and locate the mounting bracket and assembly components. Identify the mounting plate (A), curved rod (B) and spacer (C). The plate attaches to BactoLink, the curved rod holds it in place, and the spacer maintains the distance between rod and plate. Locate the two screws and washers in the antenna package. Position the mounting plate on BactoLink. Insert the screws through the plate into BactoLink, with washers between the screw heads and plate. Tighten with a 5 mm Allen key until securely attached. Locate the two flanged nuts. Position the curved rod and spacer on the plate in the desired orientation. Insert the two flanged nuts onto the threaded ends of the curved rod. Hand-tighten, or use a 13 mm wrench, until the nuts do not move and BactoLink is securely attached.

Check that the instrument runs software 2.2 or later. For an upgrade, contact support@bnovate.com. Scan the 2D barcode on the back of the antenna. Enter the username and password previously chosen for BactoHub. If you need an account, contact support. Power off the instrument. Connect the devices as described in Instrument connections and Connecting the antenna and PoE injector. Power on the device. Open Home → System Settings → Network. Activate DHCP if necessary. Wait before restarting Do not power cycle the instrument immediately. Open Home → System Settings → System Services. Activate HTTPS for WebUI access and assign port 443. If changed, reboot BactoSense. HTTPS is required for BactoLink to function. Power cycle the instrument, or first perform the optional next step. If GUI relay is needed, activate VNC, assigned to port 5900, under System Services. Then power cycle the instrument. Remote screen visibility With GUI relay, your screen actions are visible to people at the instrument and remotely connected users. Confidential information might be shared. Configure BactoLink using its serial number and a user-friendly name. Click Connect. Wait until the instrument is connected, then click Finish. The instrument appears in the BactoHub instrument list. Choose WebUI or GUI relay. The connection opens in a separate tab and remains valid for 30 minutes. Reconnect after that period.

Click Initialize BactoLink below My Instruments. Enter the instrument serial number and a user-friendly name, then press Continue. Repeat steps 2–9 of First installation. You can then access the instrument through WebUI and GUI relay.

The WebUI provides access to instrument data through the RJ45 port. Click WebUI in BactoHub to establish a connection through BactoLink. If you reboot BactoSense through the WebUI, reload the web page as well. Password​ When prompted, enter the BactoSense device username (Basic, Advanced, Admin or Service) and its chosen password. Dashboard​ The dashboard provides the latest measurement results, instrument status and warnings for expired cartridges. Dotplots​ Dotplots show an animation of recent measurements. Loading can take time, depending on the connection. Start with animation speed 1; use higher speeds once the images are fully loaded. Download options are available in GIF and FCS formats. Results​ Results show measurements over time and provide download options. Below the plot are download areas for auto mode, manual mode and instrument validation. Auto and manual results are listed at the bottom. View them as a table, download cumulative ZIP files, or download IMG and FCS files for each measurement. BactoSense Multi shows only manual mode and has no time series plot. Protocol Log​ The Protocol Log shows executed protocols and error messages. Download the data as CSV. Error Log​ The Error Log lists errors and warnings, downloadable as XLSX, CSV or PDF. System Info​ System Info provides general system information and allows screenshots to be taken. Settings​ Settings allows changes to sample names, measurement intervals and instrument name. It is unavailable for BactoSense Multi.

GUI relay provides remote desktop access as if you were physically present at the instrument. Remote screen visibility Your screen actions are visible to people at the instrument and remotely connected users. Confidential information might be shared.

If the instrument was turned off during installation, BactoLink should work immediately. If issues persist: Make sure BactoLink is fully powered on before powering on BactoSense. Allow at least 3 minutes for the instrument to establish a network connection. Check mobile network connectivity at the location using your mobile phone. If no connection is possible, disconnect and reconnect the antenna from the PoE injector to power cycle the antenna. Inspect all connections on the injector and connected instruments. If problems persist, power cycle BactoSense.

The Cleaning Kit deep-cleans the fluidic system and manual sampling device of BactoSense. Its reagents clear biological and non-biological contamination arising from the instrument's intended use. Effectiveness against contamination from other applications cannot be guaranteed. Attempts to clean with other chemicals or materials are the user's sole responsibility. Store the kit at 2–25 °C, in the dark. Under these conditions, the shelf-life is one year. The kit provides five biological and five non-biological decontaminations.

Wear protective gloves In case of skin contact, rinse immediately and abundantly with fresh water. In case of pain or irritation, consult a doctor. Wear protective safety glasses In case of eye contact, flush eyes immediately with flowing water for 10–15 minutes, holding eyelids apart, and consult a doctor. Toxic, irritating and corrosive reagents Some reagents are toxic or irritating. Wear protective equipment; do not ingest or inhale. Some reagents are corrosive to metals. Follow instructions Carefully follow this manual and the BactoSense user manual.

Safety data sheets are available from bNovate or your local distribution partner upon request.

Indications Protocol The manual sampling device may have been contaminated through improper storage; the instrument stopped in an error state with a loaded sample; or persistent biological contamination cannot be cleared with the Wash Station. Biological contamination Visible deposits on the sampling needle; frequent High baseline in SSC or Air bubble detection warnings; or electronic noise in the dotplots much higher than usual, exceeding 4 on the FL1 axis. Non-biological contamination
documents.s: When to use the Cleaning Kit

documents.t: This protocol clears biological contamination from the instrument and manual sampling device. Duration and materials Approximately 20 minutes. Requires one alcohol wipe, one Decontamination solution, one Rinsing solution and one Tube holder. Protect yourself when handling reagents Carefully follow the instructions and wear protective gloves and safety glasses. Make sure the manual sampling device is tightly installed on BactoSense. Unpack an alcohol wipe. Wipe the needle from top to bottom to remove contaminants. Let it dry for 30 seconds. Take a Decontamination solution tube and Tube holder. Remove their caps and insert the opened tube into the holder. Attach the holder containing the tube to the manual sampling device. Use the whole reagent tube Insert the entire tube, rather than pouring its reagents into the holder. Open Home → Manual mode → Start. Select Prime in Protocol and configure two replications in Replications. Press Next and Start. After both Prime processes finish, remove the holder and discard the Decontamination solution tube. Uncap a Rinsing solution tube, insert the entire tube into the holder and attach the holder to the manual sampling device. Press New, or open Home → Manual mode → Start again. Select Prime, with two replications. Press Next and Start. After both Prime processes finish, remove the holder and discard the Rinsing solution tube. Close the holder with its cap and return it to the Cleaning Kit box. The decontamination sequence is complete. Follow After cleaning.

This protocol clears non-biological contamination from the instrument and manual sampling device. Duration and materials Approximately 3.5 hours. Requires one alcohol wipe, one Cleaning solution, one Rinsing solution and one Tube holder. Protect yourself when handling reagents Carefully follow the instructions and wear protective gloves and safety glasses. Make sure the manual sampling device is tightly installed on BactoSense. Unpack an alcohol wipe. Wipe the needle from top to bottom to remove contaminants. Let it dry for 30 seconds. Take a Cleaning solution tube and Tube holder. Remove their caps, insert the entire opened tube into the holder, as illustrated above, and attach the holder to the manual sampling device. Open Home → Manual mode → Start. Select Prime, with two replications. Press Next and Start. After the protocols finish, wait 3 hours. Remove the holder and discard the Cleaning solution tube. Uncap a Rinsing solution tube, insert the entire tube into the holder and attach it to the manual sampling device. Press New, or open Home → Manual mode → Start again. Select Prime, with three replications. Press Next and Start. After all three Prime processes finish, remove the holder and discard the Rinsing solution tube. Close the holder with its cap and return it to the Cleaning Kit box. The decontamination sequence is complete.

Prime before the next sample To measure a sample now, attach it to the sampling device and first perform two Prime processes. This ensures the highest accuracy of your results. If you do not plan to measure samples, attach a clean, empty tube or the Wash Station. Perform two Prime processes before measuring the next sample.
This Quick Guide helps you get started with BactoSense, your solution for the automated measurement of the concentration of microorganisms in water.

Follow the user manual instructions Read the BactoSense user manual before installing or operating the instrument. Pay particular attention to the safety chapter and the safety information throughout the manual. Make sure you always have access to the user manual. Find the latest instrument and accessory manuals at www.bnovate.com/docs.
Parameter Range Temperature 5–30 °C (41–86 °F) Humidity 10–90 % RH Location Indoor use, maximum 2000 m (6600 ft) above sea level

Parameter Range Auto mode, at the online sampling device inlet Flow rate 200–400 mL/min (0.05–0.10 gal/min); pressure maximum 0.5 bar (7.3 psi) Temperature 5–40 °C (41–104 °F) Turbidity 0–10 FTU, 0–10 FNU Conductivity 0–100,000 μS/cm at 20 °C Chlorine Maximum 3 mg/L Iron Maximum 200 μg/L Manganese Maximum 50 μg/L pH 5–12

To measure automatically and at predefined intervals from a connected water source: Make sure the correct online sampling device is installed and the sample conditions are met. In the Home menu, press Auto mode and Start. On the time series graph view, press Start. Select Online Sampling Device (with Backflush) and configure the measurement series. Follow the on-screen instructions to start measuring.

To measure individual grab samples collected in sample tubes: Make sure the manual sampling device is installed correctly. In the Home menu, press Manual mode and Start. Select Water analysis and configure the measurement. Attach a 5 mL sample tube containing a 2–5 mL water sample to the sampling device. Follow the on-screen instructions to start the measurement.
In the Home menu, press Results (Manual) or Results (Auto) and select the desired measurement.

The cartridge contains all the reagents needed for measurements and self-cleaning. Icons in the top bar indicate the filling level of a cartridge. Find the expiration date and storage conditions on the cartridge or under System Info. Arrange a cartridge refill once the level is low or the cartridge is about to expire. To install, remove or exchange a cartridge, press Maintenance → Cartridge change and follow the on-screen instructions.
Careful decommissioning, transport, storage and recommissioning are essential. Consult Storage, transport and disposal.

BactoSense is calibration free. For operating environments requiring system suitability testing, use the System Suitability Test Kit (SST Kit). For other environments, an instrument qualification using the Validation Kit is recommended: After shipping or other long-distance transport exposing the instrument to vibration or shock. After storing the instrument for more than one month. If there are indications that measurement results could be erroneous.

The Wash Station keeps the manual sampling device clean. Use it: Before switching BactoSense off. After measuring a highly concentrated sample. If the instrument will be idle for more than six hours. If the manual sampling device has been newly installed. The Cleaning Kit clears biological and non-biological contaminations. Use it: When facing persistent contamination. If the needle of the manual sampling device has visible deposits. After stopping in an error state with a loaded sample. If High baseline or Air bubble detection warnings frequently appear.

Icon Meaning and action The last measurement triggered an alarm. Maintenance is required. Arrange a maintenance visit. No cartridge, or cartridge not initialised correctly. Install the cartridge with the on-screen instructions. Resolve the issue, then manually clear the error in the error log.
Contact bNovate customer service at support@bnovate.com or your local customer service partner.

According to United States Pharmacopeia USP <1058>, the System Suitability Test (SST) verifies that a system performs in accordance with the criteria set forth in the test procedure. The SST Kit for AQU@Sense MB is a reagent kit used to conduct this performance verification. Prerequisites: AQU@Sense MB with the manual sampling device installed. SST Kit stored under adequate conditions and not expired. A personal instrument login with Advanced or Admin permissions. Store the kit refrigerated at 2–8 °C (35–47 °F), away from light. Under these conditions, the shelf-life is one year. The kit provides 10 tests.

Wear protective gloves In case of skin contact, rinse immediately and abundantly with fresh water. In case of pain or irritation, consult a doctor. Wear protective safety glasses In case of eye contact, flush eyes immediately with flowing water for 10–15 minutes, holding eyelids apart, and consult a doctor. Read the instructions before use Carefully follow this manual and the AQU@Sense MB operating manual.

Item Quantity SDS document number Use Alcohol Wipes 10 — Single use Beads Solution 10 50106 Single use Reference Solution 10 — Single use Sterile Solution 10 — Single use Tube Holder 1 — Multiple uses Discard single-use items according to local waste disposal regulations. Safety data sheets are available from BWT upon request.

Perform an SST: As part of quality assurance and validation, for example during operational qualification, performance qualification, cartridge change or servicing. After storing the instrument for more than one month. If there are indications that measurement results could be erroneous. The procedure consists of three parts, performed in order: Optical Validation, Reference Validation and Sterile Validation. All test acceptance criteria must be met. The procedure takes approximately 2.5 hours.
documents.s: When to use the System Suitability Test Kit

documents.t: Verify that the SST Kit has not expired and has been stored under the specified conditions. Remove one alcohol wipe, one Beads Solution, one Reference Solution, one Sterile Solution and the Tube Holder. Make sure the manual sampling device is tightly installed on AQU@Sense MB. Unpack the alcohol wipe. Wipe the sampling needle from top to bottom to remove contaminants. Let it dry for 30 seconds. Log in on AQU@Sense MB with your personal username and password. Advanced or Admin permissions are required. Open Home → Maintenance → Instrument validation. Check Activate Instrument validation and press Save. Continue with Part A.

This tests the instrument's optical system by measuring a solution containing fluorescent particles. Attach the wash station to the manual sampling device. Open Home → Manual mode → Start. Select Clean Sampling Device with Washstation, with one replication. Press Next and start the protocol. After completion, shake the Beads Solution tube vigorously for 10 seconds, by hand or using a vortex mixer. Remove the caps from the Beads Solution tube and Tube Holder. Insert the opened tube into the holder. Remove the wash station and attach the holder containing the Beads Solution. Use the whole reagent tube Insert the entire reagent tube into the Tube Holder, rather than pouring its contents into the holder. Return to the protocol overview. Select Prime, with one replication. Press Next and start. After completion, return to the protocol overview. Select Beads Analysis, with one replication. Press Next and start. Review the results. All the following criteria must be met: TCC: 50,000–75,000/mL Channel CV (%) Median FL1 Less than 15 5.7–6.5 FL2 Less than 20 5.1–5.7 SSC Less than 25 4.7–6.3 If the test passes, remove the holder, remove the Beads Solution tube, close its cap and discard it. Continue with Part B. If it fails, repeat, making sure the Beads Solution is well mixed. If failures persist, contact BWT support.

This tests the instrument's automated staining process. Attach the wash station to the manual sampling device. Open Home → Manual mode → Start. Run Clean Sampling Device with Washstation, with one replication. Press Next and start. Remove the cap from a Reference Solution tube and insert the entire tube into the holder, as shown in Part A. After the cleaning protocol finishes, remove the wash station and attach the holder containing the Reference Solution. Return to the protocol overview. Run Prime, with one replication. After completion, return to the protocol overview. Select Water Analysis, with one replication. In Gates, select ICC Default Gate. Press Next and start. Compare the main bacteria clouds to the reference criteria: Dotplot Acceptance criterion FL1 / FL2 Main cloud above 4.5 on the FL1 axis and below 5 on the FL2 axis FL1 / SSC Main cloud above 2 and below 5.5 on the SSC axis Appearance of the clouds Depending on the cartridge and storage conditions, the clouds may differ from the example. If the test passes, remove the holder, remove the Reference Solution tube, close its cap and discard it. Continue with Part C. If it fails, repeat with a fresh Reference Solution. If failures persist, contact BWT support.

This verifies the cleanliness of the sampling device and fluidic system by measuring cell-free water. Attach the wash station to the manual sampling device. Open Home → Manual mode → Start. Run Clean Sampling Device with Washstation, with one replication. Press Next and start. Remove the cap from a Sterile Solution tube and insert the entire tube into the holder, as shown in Part A. After the cleaning protocol finishes, remove the wash station and attach the holder containing the Sterile Solution. Return to the protocol overview. Run Prime, with one replication. After completion, return to the protocol overview. Select Water Analysis, with one replication. Select ICC Default Gate, press Next and start. Review the result. The acceptance criterion is ICC less than 100/mL. If the test passes, remove the holder, remove the Sterile Solution tube, close its cap and discard it. Return the holder to the SST Kit, store the kit under the specified conditions, and attach the wash station to the manual sampling device. If it fails, perform biological decontamination using the Cleaning Kit. Repeat with a fresh Sterile Solution. If failures persist, contact BWT support. Open Home → Maintenance → Instrument validation. Uncheck Activate Instrument validation and press Save. You have successfully completed the System Suitability Test when all three parts have passed.

The Validation Kit is a reagent kit used to validate the proper functioning of BactoSense. Its reagents have been developed for use after measuring drinking water samples. The kit may not be effective if stored under inadequate conditions, if expired, or if samples other than drinking water have been measured. Store the kit refrigerated at 2–8 °C (35–47 °F), away from light. Under these conditions, the shelf-life is one year. The kit provides 10 validations.

Wear protective gloves In case of skin contact, rinse immediately and abundantly with fresh water. In case of pain or irritation, consult a doctor. Wear protective safety glasses In case of eye contact, flush eyes immediately with flowing water for 10–15 minutes, holding eyelids apart, and consult a doctor. Read the instructions before use Carefully follow this manual and the BactoSense user manual.

Perform an instrument validation: After shipping or other long-distance transport with vibration or shock. After storing the instrument for more than one month. If there are indications that measurement results could be erroneous. The full validation consists of three parts, performed in order: Optical Validation, Reference Validation and Sterile Validation. All acceptance criteria must be met. A full validation takes approximately 3 hours. In specific cases, a partial validation can be performed. Complete the preparations first, then follow the relevant part.
documents.s: When to use the Validation Kit

documents.t: Verify that the kit has not expired and has been stored under the specified conditions. For a full validation, remove one alcohol wipe, one Beads Solution, one Reference Solution, one Sterile Solution and the Tube Holder. For a partial validation, take only the wipe, Tube Holder and relevant solution. Make sure the manual sampling device is tightly installed on BactoSense. Unpack the alcohol wipe. Wipe the sampling needle from top to bottom to remove contaminants. Let it dry for 30 seconds. Log in as Admin. From Home → Maintenance → Self-check, press Rerun. Verify that every test displays a green PASS. Open Home → Maintenance → Instrument validation. Check Activate Instrument validation and press Save. For a full validation, continue with Part A. For a partial validation, continue with the corresponding part.

This tests the optical system by measuring a solution containing fluorescent particles. Complete the preparations if not already done. Attach the wash station to the manual sampling device. If none is available, attach an empty, clean 5 mL screw-cap tube. As Admin, open Home → Manual mode → Start. Select Clean Sampling Device with Washstation, with one replication. Without a wash station, select Clean Sampling Device, with two replications. Press Next and start the protocol. After completion, shake the Beads Solution tube vigorously for 10 seconds, by hand or using a vortex mixer. Remove the caps from the Beads Solution tube and Tube Holder. Insert the opened tube into the holder. Remove the wash station and attach the holder containing the Beads Solution to the manual sampling device. Use the whole reagent tube Insert the entire reagent tube into the Tube Holder, rather than pouring its contents into the holder. Open Home → Manual mode → Start. Select Prime, with one replication. Press Next and start. Return to the protocol overview. Select Beads Analysis, with two replications. Press Next and start. Review the results. All the following criteria must be met: TCC: 50,000–75,000/mL Channel CV (%) Median FL1 Less than 15 5.7–6.5 FL2 Less than 20 5.1–5.7 SSC Less than 25 4.7–6.3 If the test passes, remove the Tube Holder, remove the Beads Solution tube, close its cap and discard it. Continue with Part B. If it fails, check the kit's expiry and storage conditions, then repeat, making sure the Beads Solution is well mixed. If failures persist, contact bNovate support or your local service representative.

This validates the automated staining process. Complete the preparations if performing this part alone. Attach the wash station, or an empty, clean 5 mL screw-cap tube if no wash station is available. As Admin, open Home → Manual mode → Start. Run Clean Sampling Device with Washstation, with one replication. Without a wash station, run Clean Sampling Device, with two replications. Press Next and start. Uncap the Reference Solution tube and insert the entire tube into the Tube Holder, as shown in Part A. Remove the wash station and attach the holder containing the Reference Solution. Open Home → Manual mode → Start. Run Prime, with one replication. Return to the protocol overview. Select Water Analysis, with two replications. In Gates, select the default gate for the cartridge type, for example ICC Default Gate or TCC Default Gate. Press Next and start. Compare the main bacteria clouds to the reference criteria: Dotplot Acceptance criterion FL1 / FL2 Main cloud above 4.5 on the FL1 axis and below 5 on the FL2 axis FL1 / SSC Main cloud above 2 and below 5.5 on the SSC axis Appearance of the clouds Depending on the cartridge and storage conditions, the clouds may differ from the example. If the test passes, remove the Tube Holder, remove the Reference Solution tube, close its cap and discard it. Continue with Part C. If it fails, check the kit's expiry and storage conditions. Repeat with a fresh Reference Solution. If failures persist, contact bNovate support or your local service representative.

This validates the cleanliness of BactoSense by measuring cell-free water. Complete the preparations if performing this part alone. Attach the wash station, or an empty, clean 5 mL screw-cap tube if no wash station is available. As Admin, open Home → Manual mode → Start. Run Clean Sampling Device with Washstation, with one replication. Without a wash station, run Clean Sampling Device, with two replications. Press Next and start. Uncap the Sterile Solution tube and insert the entire tube into the Tube Holder, as shown in Part A. Remove the wash station and attach the holder containing the Sterile Solution. Open Home → Manual mode → Start. Run Prime, with one replication. Return to the protocol overview. Select Water Analysis, with two replications. In Gates, select ICC Default Gate or TCC Default Gate, according to the cartridge. Press Next and start. Review the results. The applicable criterion must be met: Cartridge Acceptance criterion TCC TCC less than 300/mL ICC ICC less than 100/mL If the test passes, remove the Tube Holder, remove the Sterile Solution tube, close its cap and discard it. Return the holder to the Validation Kit and attach the wash station to the manual sampling device. If it fails, check the kit's expiry and storage conditions. Perform biological decontamination, then repeat with a fresh Sterile Solution. If failures persist, contact bNovate support or your local service representative. Open Home → Maintenance → Instrument validation. Uncheck Activate Instrument validation and press Save. You have successfully validated your instrument when all required parts have passed.
